Findings-mode verification pass, NOT a build-quality score. This is for a colleague's already-open PR review (PR #84, Zimmermann PWA Kit repo, "fix(app): remove placeholder DntNotification modal (SFCC-863)"). Several findings were produced by me and by two other review agents. Before any of these reach the human reviewer (Marcel) as review comments, verify each one: reproduce it or say you could not. Return CONFIRMED (reproduced from source), PLAUSIBLE (consistent with what you read, decisive evidence missing — say what would settle it), or UNSUPPORTED (the citation doesn't support the claim — say what's actually true). Downgrade anything whose conclusion is broader than its evidence supports.

**Important: use the TRUE current PR head, not an older snapshot.** The PR moved during this review (a merge commit was pushed partway through). Current head SHA is `da8c37036d03d0fcaaffeb586573d20d9bf9ae63` on branch `fix/SFCC-863-remove-dnt-placeholder-modal`. A worktree already checked out at this exact commit (with `node_modules` symlinked, `npx tsc`/`npx vitest`/`npx eslint` all runnable) is at:
`/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/315b63a0-b125-4f80-a22b-5eb85ce56fd5/scratchpad/pr84-head`
The PR's base (develop at merge-base) is at:
`/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-marcel-a-n-navarro-Dev-zimmermann-pwa/315b63a0-b125-4f80-a22b-5eb85ce56fd5/scratchpad/pr84-base` (commit `9ab9aad5a75158231988a9ca0816b4fe877e1137`)
`gh pr view 84` / `gh pr diff 84` / `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/pulls/84/...` all work if you need live GitHub state (reviews, comments, statuses).

I already confirmed myself (don't just take my word for it, spot-check at least the registry one and the responsive-import one since they're the highest-stakes claims): tsc is clean and vitest is 46 files/691 tests all passing at this true head.

## Findings to verify

**1. [Process] Zero qualifying human approval currently exists on the PR.**
Claim: `overrides/app/components/_app/` is a Tier 2 "Global Shell" path per `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md` (also `overrides/app/components/_app/index.test.tsx`, its sibling). CODEOWNERS routes it to `@ZimmermannAU/pwa-squad-a @ZimmermannAU/pwa-squad-b @ZimmermannAU/tier-2-approvers @ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` (any one satisfies GitHub's CODEOWNERS check). The PR author, TimLavelleACC, replied in-thread to CodeRabbit's Tier-2-review-process question with "I am a Tier1 approver and the overall solution architect on this program of work, so this is approved given I have made the change" — but GitHub does not allow a PR author to submit an "Approved" review on their own PR (a hard platform restriction, not a CODEOWNERS nuance), and separately, being a Tier-1-approver doesn't substitute for the Tier-2 "developer other than the author" requirement — these are different gates. CodeRabbit's own review thread (`gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/pulls/84/comments`) explicitly told the author this doesn't satisfy the requirement. Marcel (marcelannavarro) DID submit a review — `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/pulls/84/reviews` shows `{"author":"marcelannavarro","commit_id":"50871bf...","state":"DISMISSED","body":"LGTM!"}` — but it's on the OLD head commit (`50871bf`) and its state is DISMISSED (GitHub auto-dismisses stale approvals when new commits land — the branch got a new commit, `da8c37036`, a merge of develop, after Marcel's review). Verify: (a) is `50871bf` genuinely not an ancestor-equivalent of `da8c37036` in a way that would make the dismissal spurious — i.e. did the merge commit change anything real, or was it a no-op merge that GitHub dismissed the review over unnecessarily? (b) is there any other approving review from anyone else I might have missed? (c) confirm the current overall PR review-decision state via `gh pr view 84 --json reviewDecision`.

**2. [Correctness, high-confidence] `overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx` imports `HideOnDesktop`/`HideOnMobile` from the base SFCC path instead of the already-overridden local one.**
Claim: line ~49 reads `import { HideOnDesktop, HideOnMobile } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/responsive';` but `overrides/app/components/responsive/index.tsx` is a real, already-existing Zimmermann override that changes the desktop/mobile breakpoint split from Chakra's default (`lg`, 992px) to `md` (768px) — a genuine behavioral divergence, not a cosmetic port. This is exactly the failure mode SFCC-863's own ticket text warns about for Header/Footer/DrawerMenu/ListMenu (which the PR correctly imports via relative paths, e.g. `import Header from '../header'`) — but this 5th already-overridden dependency in the same file was missed. Also claimed: `overrides/app/components/_app/index.test.tsx`'s own `vi.mock()` for `responsive` mocks the SAME wrong base-SFCC path, meaning the test suite passing does not catch this. Verify by reading the actual import line, confirming `overrides/app/components/responsive/index.tsx` exists and genuinely diverges in behavior from Chakra's default breakpoint (not just existing but identical to base), and confirming the test file's mock path.

**3. [Process, high-stakes] The auto-generated registry files are corrupted at the CURRENT true PR head, contradicting the PR's own "APPROVED" status.**
Claim: `.claude/registry/components.md` at commit `da8c37036` has TWO `> Last updated:` header lines (`2026-09-04T00:54:34.181Z` and `2026-09-02T10:17:24.916Z`) and a duplicated, self-contradictory `App` row — one says `App | Override | overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx | ... | 21` consumers, immediately followed by `App | Base | app/components/_app/index.jsx | ... | 7` consumers (i.e., the registry now asserts `_app` both is and isn't overridden — the literal subject of this PR). `.claude/registry/hooks.md` similarly has duplicated `useEinstein` and `useToast` rows with different values. This resulted from a botched resolution of the merge-conflict I'd earlier diagnosed as "just re-run the generator" (the merge commit `da8c37036` merges `develop` into this branch). CodeRabbit's own review on commit `da8c37036` (`gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/pulls/84/reviews`, filter `commit_id == "da8c37036..."`) shows TWO reviews 16 seconds apart: `CHANGES_REQUESTED` at 04:16:03 explicitly citing this exact duplication in both files by name, then `APPROVED` (empty body) at 04:16:19 — on the IDENTICAL commit, with no commit pushed in between. Verify: (a) read `.claude/registry/components.md` and `hooks.md` directly at commit `da8c37036` yourself and confirm the duplication is real and matches this description (don't trust my line numbers, re-find them), (b) confirm via the GitHub API that both those reviews really are 16 seconds apart on the same commit_id with nothing pushed in between, (c) form a view on whether characterizing this as "CodeRabbit approved a PR containing a defect it had itself just flagged, without the defect being fixed" is an accurate description or overstated.

**4. [Minor] PR body's self-reported test count doesn't match reality.**
Claim: PR body's test-plan checklist says "Full suite: `npx vitest run` — 47 files / 682 tests passing." Actual measured: 46 files/680 tests at the original head (`50871bf`), 46 files/691 tests at the true current head (`da8c37036`, after the develop merge added ~11 more tests from an unrelated already-merged PR). The PR's own CI bot comment (`vitest-summary`, visible via `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/issues/84/comments`) independently reports "680/680 passed" for the original commit — matching my count, not the PR body's. Verify the CI bot comment text and confirm the discrepancy is real (this is a very minor, non-blocking finding — just confirm it's accurately characterized as "PR body inaccurate by 1 file/2 tests," not something worse or a non-issue).

**5. [Should NOT be a finding — confirm this] The disputed `useAppOrigin` "default import instead of named export, crashed SSR" claim in the PR body.**
This should NOT be reported as a confirmed defect either way — I want you to confirm that both the base file and the new file use identical, correct named-import syntax (`import {useAppOrigin} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-app-origin'` in base, `import { useAppOrigin } from ...` in new — same thing, prettier-reformatted), meaning there is no delta in the shipped diff corresponding to this claimed bug/fix. Confirm this is correctly classified as "unverifiable from repository artifacts, since there's only one commit and no intermediate state" rather than either "confirmed true" or "confirmed false."

For each of the 5 items, give me a verdict and, where you downgrade something, say exactly what specific evidence is missing or wrong. Keep the report structured by finding number. This PR is small; don't expand scope beyond verifying these 5 specific claims.

content.text:
## Findings-mode verification — PR #84 (`fix/SFCC-863-remove-dnt-placeholder-modal`, head `da8c37036`)

All verification below was done by reading the actual files at `da8c37036` in the provided worktree, running `npx vitest run` myself, pulling raw GitHub API state (reviews, review comments, timeline events, branch protection, workflow logs), and diffing exact commits. Nothing here is taken on the word of the earlier findings.

---

### Finding 1 — Zero qualifying human approval currently exists

**Verdict: CONFIRMED** (all three sub-questions)

- CODEOWNERS confirmed verbatim: `CODEOWNERS:91` routes `overrides/app/components/_app/` to `@ZimmermannAU/pwa-squad-a @ZimmermannAU/pwa-squad-b @ZimmermannAU/tier-2-approvers @ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`.
- TimLavelleACC's two review-thread replies ("I am a Tier1 approver... this is approved given I have made the change," comments `3929991676`/`3929991674` region) both landed as top-level review **state `COMMENTED`** (review ids `5108210204`, `5108210741`) — never `APPROVED`, consistent with GitHub's hard block on self-approval.
- CodeRabbit's rebuttal (comment `3929998360`, full text retrieved) after running its own live `gh pr view`/`gh api` check: *"Your Tier 1 approval does not satisfy the independent-review requirement because you are the PR author... Please add approval from a developer in the other squad."* — matches the claim essentially word-for-word.
- Marcel's review (`5109083112`, `state: DISMISSED`, body `"LGTM!"`, `commit_id: 50871bf...`) is the only human `APPROVED` review that has ever existed on this PR — confirmed by paging through all 9 reviews; no other human approval exists anywhere.
- **(a) Was the dismissal spurious (no-op merge)?** No. `git show 50871bf:.claude/registry/components.md` shows the registry was **clean** at Marcel's reviewed commit (one `Last updated` line, one `App` row). At `da8c37036` it's corrupted (see Finding 3). I also confirmed via `gh api .../pulls/84/files` that GitHub's own merge-base-relative "files changed" list is exactly the original 6 PR files (registries + `_app` x2 + `vendor.d.ts` + `vitest.config.ts`) — the `_app/index.tsx`/`index.test.tsx` files are byte-identical between `50871bf` and `da8c37036` (absent from that commit-pair's diff entirely). So the *only* thing that changed between what Marcel approved and current head is the registry corruption — a real, new, defective change, not noise. The dismissal was warranted, not spurious.
- Mechanism confirmed as automatic, not manual: `develop` branch protection has `dismiss_stale_reviews: true`; the timeline event for Marcel's dismissal (`issues/events/30531319837`) shows `dismissal_message: null`, `dismissal_commit_id: da8c37036...` — the standard signature of GitHub's auto-dismissal-on-push, not a deliberate click.
- **(b)** No other approving review missed — confirmed above.
- **(c)** `gh pr view 84 --json reviewDecision` → `"REVIEW_REQUIRED"`. Also `mergeStateStatus: "BLOCKED"`, `mergeable: "MERGEABLE"` — blocked specifically on review policy.

*Aside, not one of the 5 claims, flagged only because I saw it while pulling this data:* the `QA` check itself currently shows `conclusion: "failure"` on `da8c37036` (the `Storybook interaction & a11y tests` job specifically; `Unit tests (Vitest)` passed). Worth Marcel's attention independent of the review-approval question, but I did not investigate further — out of this pass's scope.

---

### Finding 2 — Wrong-path `HideOnDesktop`/`HideOnMobile` import

**Verdict: CONFIRMED, high confidence**

- `overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx:49`: `import { HideOnDesktop, HideOnMobile } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/responsive';` (used at lines 405/415/417/424).
- `overrides/app/components/responsive/index.tsx` is real and genuinely diverges: its own header comment states base hardcodes `lg` (992px) while this override uses `MOBILE_DESKTOP_SPLIT = 'md'` (768px) "everywhere else (header, footer, mega menu)."
- Confirmed against the actual base file (`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/responsive/index.jsx`): both `HideOnDesktop` and `HideOnMobile` there use `lg` — so this is a genuine behavioral divergence, not a no-op override.
- `overrides/app/components/_app/index.test.tsx:82`: `vi.mock('@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/responsive', () => ({` — the test mocks the same wrong base path, so the suite passing is not evidence against this defect.

---

### Finding 3 — Corrupted registry at current true head, approved anyway

**Verdict: CONFIRMED, all sub-parts**

- `.claude/registry/components.md:3-4`: two `Last updated` lines (`2026-09-04T00:54:34.181Z`, `2026-09-02T10:17:24.916Z`) — exact match.
- `.claude/registry/components.md:12-13`: contradictory `App` rows — `Override | ... | 21` immediately followed by `Base | ... | 7` — exact match.
- `.claude/registry/hooks.md:3-4`: same duplicated timestamps.
- `.claude/registry/hooks.md:33-34`: duplicate `useEinstein` rows, consumers `2` vs `1` — confirmed.
- `.claude/registry/hooks.md:73-74`: duplicate `useToast` rows, consumers `2` vs `0` — confirmed.
- Bonus corroboration not named in the original claim: `hooks.md:19-21` also shows a duplicated `useContentful`/`useCleanupTemporaryBaskets` interleaving — the corruption is broader than the two named examples, which strengthens rather than undercuts the finding.
- Confirmed via `git show 50871bf:...` that both files were clean at the pre-merge commit — the corruption was introduced specifically by the merge commit `da8c37036`, consistent with a botched conflict resolution.
- **(b)** Timing confirmed via API: review `5109123495` (`CHANGES_REQUESTED`, `2026-09-04T04:16:03Z`) explicitly names this exact defect ("Both files append a second older registry snapshot... `components.md#L4-L4`... `hooks.md#L4-L4`"); review `5109124615` (`APPROVED`, empty body, `2026-09-04T04:16:19Z`) follows 16 seconds later. Both carry `commit_id: da8c37036...`, and the full commit list for this PR contains only `50871bf` and `da8c37036` — nothing pushed in between.
- **(c)** My view: accurate, not overstated. I independently re-read the files at `da8c37036` myself (not trusting line numbers given to me) and the exact defect CodeRabbit flagged in `CHANGES_REQUESTED` is still there 16 seconds later when it approved. This is a reproducible tool inconsistency worth surfacing to Marcel as-is.

---

### Finding 4 — PR body test-count mismatch

**Verdict: CONFIRMED, with one precision correction**

- PR body: *"Full suite: `npx vitest run` — 47 files / 682 tests passing."*
- Raw workflow log for the QA run against the **original** head `50871bf` (run `33823788293`, step "Unit tests (Vitest)", `2026-09-04T00:58:48Z`): `Test Files 46 passed (46)` / `Tests 680 passed (680)` — sourced directly from the workflow's own log text.
- My own `npx vitest run` at the **true current** head (`da8c37036`): `Test Files 46 passed (46)` / `Tests 691 passed (691)` — matches the prompt's figure exactly.
- **Correction:** the `<!-- vitest-summary -->` issue comment (id `5534146565`) has `created_at: 2026-09-04T00:58:49Z` but `updated_at: 2026-09-04T04:18:50Z` — it was edited in place by the later QA run and **now displays "691/691 passed,"** not 680/680. So the claim that "the CI bot comment independently reports 680/680" is true only of that comment's original, since-overwritten content — anyone opening the PR thread right now will see 691/691, not 680/680. The underlying fact (46/680 was the true count at the original head, vs. the PR body's 47/682) is still solid — just now sourced from the raw workflow log rather than the (no-longer-accurate) visible comment.
- Net: PR body is inaccurate by exactly 1 file / 2 tests relative to the commit its own test-plan describes. Confirmed as stated — not worse (no hidden failures either count) and not a non-issue.

---

### Finding 5 — Disputed `useAppOrigin` import claim (should not be reported as a defect)

**Verdict: CONFIRMED as correctly classified — unverifiable, not true-or-false**

- Base (`node_modules/.../app/components/_app/index.jsx:23`): `import {useAppOrigin} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-app-origin'`
- New (`overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx:17`, true head): `import { useAppOrigin } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-app-origin';`
- Identical named import of the same module/identifier; only Prettier whitespace/semicolon formatting differs. The hook module (`use-app-origin.js`) exports `useAppOrigin` as a **named export only** — so a default import would indeed resolve to `undefined` and crash on call, meaning the claimed failure mode is mechanically plausible in the abstract — but:
- `git log --all --oneline -- overrides/app/components/_app/index.tsx` returns exactly **one** commit in all of history: `50871bf`. There is no earlier override version, no intermediate commit, nothing in the repo to diff against.
- Correct classification: unverifiable from repository artifacts — no commit shows a "before" state, so this cannot be confirmed true (no evidence the bug ever shipped anywhere) or confirmed false (no evidence it never existed locally, pre-commit). Recommend it stay out of the review comments as a code defect either way.

---

**Summary:** Findings 1–4 all reproduce cleanly from source with direct API/log/file evidence (Finding 4 needed one correction to *which artifact* currently shows the number, not to the number itself). Finding 5 is correctly identified as a non-verifiable claim and should not be posted as a defect in either direction.
